title: Amanuensis roadmap: from surveyed codebase to living conspectus
northStar: Once a repository has been fully surveyed, Amanuensis maintains a revision-aware conspectus and can furnish any consequential review, design decision, or generative exploration with a bounded situation model: current facts, traced intent, applicable constraints, known contradictions, invalidated knowledge, plausible options, and explicit unknowns.
scopeDecision: The ambition is coherent as a program and too broad as a single release. Amanuensis will become the codebase epistemic engine—not a universal orchestration platform, autonomous product manager, or second source of truth for code. The first product proof is a living record that becomes stale precisely, repairs itself selectively, and reduces human verification work. Review, architecture, research learning, and Chorusmith extraction earn their place only after that proof.

baselineObservations.claim: The current product already separates scope, structural, concern, adversarial, and mapped phases, and server-side invariants limit what may be claimed at each depth.
The SQLite record already stores evidence, dispositions, findings, contradictions, cross-references, file ownership, query history, and git baselines.
Change detection currently maps changed paths to file-ledger rows and marks every entry in directly affected subsystems stale; it does not compute transitive claim or seam impact.

Finding repairs now separate fixed-pending-verification from verified-fixed, and both verification and contradiction resolution require structured evidence; append-only events preserve later reopenings and supersession history.
Access and query logs support usage-aware compression, but that mechanism optimizes retrieval rather than learning which claims remain true or which methods work.
The repository has broad mechanical validation for tools, schemas, storage, invariants, adversarial behavior, performance, and materialization.

inferences.claim: Temporal validity and targeted revalidation are the highest-leverage missing substrate.
inferences.basis: Review, architecture, and research learning all become unsafe if a changed file can leave plausible but invalid claims looking current.
inferences.counterpoint: A coarser subsystem-staleness model may prove sufficient for smaller repositories; the roadmap therefore requires comparative cost and recall measurements before deeper graph machinery is accepted.

inferences.claim: Amanuensis can support architecture work without becoming the owner of goals or decisions.
inferences.basis: Its evidence, constraints, contradictions, and history can compile the situation in which a decision is made.
inferences.counterpoint: Inferring intent from code can fossilize accidents; direct intent, inferred intent, and observed behavior must remain separate kinds.

inferences.claim: Crosswalk-driven research can improve decisions only if questions are admitted and later reconciled against their decision impact.
inferences.basis: Unbounded topic generation creates an attractive research backlog with no obligation to change a design or close a gap.
inferences.counterpoint: Some exploratory research has delayed value; the system must retain bounded speculative questions without pretending they are validated product work.

openQuestions.question: Is claim validity best represented by commit intervals, explicit supersession edges, or both?
What recall target is achievable for transitive impact without parsing every supported language?
Which design-session artifacts belong in Amanuensis custody versus Chorusmith session custody?
What evidence is sufficient to claim that imported research changed a code decision rather than merely decorating it?

tensions.name: Record versus reality
tensions.left: A durable record prevents repeated work.
tensions.right: The repository and its behavior remain the implementation truth.
tensions.resolution: Amanuensis records claims about code with validity, provenance, and invalidation; it never treats its prose as more authoritative than the referenced code state.

tensions.name: Continuity versus staleness
tensions.right: Changed code can make yesterday's knowledge dangerous.
tensions.resolution: Preserve historical claims while removing current authority until targeted revalidation succeeds.

tensions.name: Automation versus desire
tensions.left: Run the epistemic loop unattended end to end.
tensions.right: A model must not invent product goals or silently accept architecture decisions.
tensions.resolution: Automate observation, challenge, maintenance, option generation, and verification; reserve desire, irreversible policy, and decision acceptance for humans.

tensions.name: Density versus proof
tensions.left: Give reviewers and designers a high-value brief.
tensions.right: Compression can erase uncertainty and provenance.
tensions.resolution: Compile task-specific briefs from typed claims, with expandable evidence and explicit omitted/unknown sections.

tensions.name: Product identity versus platform duplication
tensions.left: Amanuensis should feel like a complete code intelligence product.
tensions.right: Chorusmith is the natural home for general session orchestration and context compilation.
tensions.resolution: Keep Amanuensis complete as a domain engine and user-facing workflow; expose stable contracts so Chorusmith can orchestrate it later without an early rewrite.

tensions.name: Immanent design versus speculative potential
tensions.left: Honor what the system is already trying to do.
tensions.right: Do not let current accidents cap its potential.
tensions.resolution: Generate three labeled lenses—immanent, adversarial, and speculative—without merging them into a false consensus.

definitions.definition: At a named commit: every in-scope file is assigned or explicitly excluded; every subsystem has completed the required phase sequence; every declared seam has both endpoints mapped and an integral assessment; every applicable concern has an evidence-backed disposition or a tracked gap; dispatched, landed, and scored work reconcile; and the clean export passes read-back validation.
negativeCriteria: It does not mean the repository contains no defects.
It does not mean every open question is answered.
It does not mean a green collection of subsystem checks proves the integrated HEAD state.

definitions.definition: The authoritative ledger of what Amanuensis has established, rejected, invalidated, or left open about a codebase, including the evidence and repository state that bound each claim.
negativeCriteria: It is not the source of truth for code behavior; code and runtime evidence remain primary.
It is not a wiki whose uncited prose becomes authoritative through repetition.
It is not a substitute for accepted product intent or architecture decisions.

definitions.definition: A system of record that detects relevant repository changes, predicts affected knowledge, withdraws stale authority, schedules bounded revalidation, records supersession, and verifies that regenerated projections match durable state.
negativeCriteria: It is not a periodic full rescan with a new timestamp.
It is not query-frequency compression mislabeled as learning.
It is not automatic rewriting of claims without retained history.

definitions.definition: A change review that combines the diff with the pre-existing conspectus, predicted blast radius, historical findings, cross-seam obligations, invalidated claims, adversarial challenge, and an integral check of the assembled HEAD state.
negativeCriteria: It is not a larger list of plausible defects.
It is not a unit-test summary.
It is not a claim of safety when known gaps or unlanded work remain.

definitions.definition: A bounded decision-support process that compiles observed behavior, direct and inferred intent, constraints, contradictions, options, consequences, falsifiers, and unresolved research into a reviewable decision record.
negativeCriteria: It does not let the model originate the user's desire.
It does not collapse evidence, interpretation, and recommendation into one voice.
It does not accept or execute an architecture decision on the user's behalf.

definitions.definition: A traceable change to corpus state, retrieval policy, method choice, research backlog, or user preference that follows from observed outcomes and can itself be revised.
negativeCriteria: It is not merely storing more text.
It is not tuning behavior from an unscored conversation.
It is not importing external research without provenance or decision relevance.

durableObjects.name: Claim
durableObjects.contract: No current authority without evidence, repository validity, and an epistemic kind; invalidation preserves history.

durableObjects.name: Crosswalk
durableObjects.contract: Relations are typed and supported; neither endpoint inherits unsupported properties from the other.

durableObjects.name: Obligation
durableObjects.contract: Every detected gap or invalidation has a destination, and blocking obligations keep the relevant gate red.

durableObjects.name: Decision
durableObjects.contract: Amanuensis may draft; only an authorized human or owning system can accept.

durableObjects.name: Run
durableObjects.contract: Every unattended run is reproducible enough to audit and reconciles intended work with landed and scored outputs.

durableObjects.name: CodebaseBrief
durableObjects.contract: Every mode projection preserves one immutable source truth; exact registry selection is model-free, and every non-selected candidate has an explicit reason.

ownership.owns: Implementation behavior, tests, history, and directly observed execution.
ownership.doesNotOwn: The explanation of why behavior exists or which future should be chosen.

ownership.owns: Codebase claims, evidence, validity, contradictions, review briefs, design situation models, and revalidation obligations.
ownership.doesNotOwn: User desire, general orchestration, external-source truth, merges, or accepted product decisions.

ownership.owns: External research sources, normalized claims, provenance, and research synthesis.
ownership.doesNotOwn: What the code does or whether external research should control a code decision.

ownership.owns: Method qualification and extraction of candidate lessons from completed work.
ownership.doesNotOwn: Automatic promotion of a candidate lesson into policy without validation and read-back.

ownership.owns: Cross-domain session orchestration, context compilation, artifact lineage, and project-type composition.
ownership.doesNotOwn: Amanuensis domain invariants or premature replacement of a working workflow.

ownership.owns: Desire, priority, risk appetite, architecture acceptance, permission boundaries, and irreversible action.
ownership.doesNotOwn: Rechecking evidence that the machine has already proven and made auditable.

unattended: Read configured repository and conspectus sources, detect changes, and update derived indexes.
Invalidate current authority, create obligations, schedule revalidation, and retain historical claims.
Generate review briefs, architecture options, adversarial challenges, research questions, and draft decision records.
Run configured tests, controls, bounded relational checks, materialization, and read-back verification.
Use already configured analysis and research providers within explicit budget, source, and data boundaries.
humanGates: A new product desire, priority, or risk appetite is required.
A data source, API, repository, spend boundary, or external audience is outside the configured envelope.
An architecture decision, policy exception, code merge, deployment, or destructive action would be accepted or executed.
Two valid options remain and the choice depends on preference rather than evidence.
hardStops: No finding, fixed status, or current claim may cross its evidence gate.
No blocking obligation may be hidden by a green aggregate status.
No run may report complete when dispatched, landed, and scored sets differ.
No generated projection may publish when state, coverage, or content read-back disagrees with durable storage.

principles.title: Temporal authority, permanent history
principles.rule: Claims can lose present authority without being deleted; supersession and invalidation are evidence-bearing events.

principles.title: Observations before interpretations
principles.rule: Every brief and record keeps observed facts, inferences, hypotheses, questions, desires, and decisions distinguishable.

principles.title: Generators do not certify themselves
principles.rule: A separate verifier checks findings, completion, projections, and high-impact recommendations; programmatic gates halt progress when feasible.

principles.title: Composition is its own proof obligation
principles.rule: Subsystem success never substitutes for fan-in reconciliation, seam review, or an integral HEAD lane.

principles.title: Unknowns have destinations
principles.rule: A gap must create a visible obligation owned by a later pass, a research queue, or a human decision; otherwise completion remains red.

principles.title: Start with explicit relations
principles.rule: Use registries, lexical structure, git history, and bounded relational cores before models, embeddings, ontologies, or graph infrastructure.

principles.title: Measure the reduction in verification burden
principles.rule: Success is not output volume; it is more correct action with less repeated human checking, without suppressing uncertainty.

stages.label: Now — make the record alive
stages.horizon: First 6–10 engineering weeks; complete before expanding the product surface.
stages.objective: Prove that a completed survey can stay trustworthy across repository changes with less work than resurveying it.
exitCriteria: The full-survey definition is computed and cannot go green with missing files, seams, dispositions, runs, or read-back mismatches.
Known claim-invalidating changes are detected and revalidated with target recall while benign changes stay below the false-invalidation guardrail.
A fixed finding cannot become verified-fixed without new evidence at the repaired revision.
An unattended refresh completes within configured authority and stops visibly at every hard gate.
The living-record path beats full resurvey on human verification minutes without worsening known-defect recall.

initiatives.title: Dogfood baseline and executable definitions
initiatives.outcome: Amanuensis can survey itself at a pinned commit, calculate whether that survey is complete, and replay a graded fixture ladder against an immutable baseline.
initiatives.rationale: The program needs a falsifiable baseline before schema work. Otherwise every later improvement can be declared successful by changing the meaning of complete.
deliverables: An ADR freezing operational meanings for fully surveyed, current, stale, invalid, resolved, verified-fixed, and complete.
A self-conspectus fixture pinned to a repository commit with inventory, seam, concern, and run reconciliation manifests.
A control harness containing null, benign, invalidating, cross-seam, incoherent-request, export, and repeated-run cases.
A baseline report with denominators, exclusions, runtime configuration, replicate IDs, and minimum detectable effects.
acceptance: The completion checker reports the named missing obligation for each independently removed file assignment, concern disposition, seam endpoint, landed result, and scored result.
Every gate is demonstrated red at least once before the green baseline is accepted.
Two unchanged-baseline runs are reported separately and establish metric step size; they are not pooled.
The baseline export is regenerated in a clean directory and read back against durable counts and identifiers.
initiatives.redGate: Delete or corrupt one obligation in each control class; if completion stays green or the error does not name the missing destination, A0 fails.
risks: A self-survey can overfit the fixture to Amanuensis's own architecture.
A single model/runtime baseline can be mistaken for a general reliability estimate.

initiatives.title: Temporal claim and supersession model
initiatives.outcome: Every authoritative statement is typed, provenance-bearing, and explicitly valid for a repository state; invalidation and supersession preserve history.
initiatives.rationale: A living record cannot be built by attaching a stale bit to whole subsystem prose. Review and design both require knowing exactly which claims lost authority and why.
deliverables: A schema ADR comparing commit intervals, supersession edges, and a combined model against real query patterns.
Additive migrations for claims, claim-evidence links, validity events, and epistemic kinds.
Write-path invariants that reject untyped authority, missing provenance, invalid commit intervals, and unsupported supersession.
A compatibility projection that maps existing entries, evidence, dispositions, contradictions, and findings without destructive migration.
acceptance: Existing databases migrate forward and retain byte-for-byte accessible legacy artifacts; rollback can ignore new tables without losing old data.
Observation, inference, hypothesis, open question, direct intent, inferred intent, and decision cannot be stored interchangeably.
A claim invalidated at commit B is not returned as current at B or later, remains queryable historically, and can be superseded only with new evidence.
Bounded exhaustive tests cover interval edges, supersession cycles, evidence reachability, and contradictory current-authority states.
initiatives.redGate: Attempt to create current authority without evidence, with an unknown commit, with a validity gap, or through a supersession cycle; every write must be rejected transactionally.
risks: Over-normalization could make ordinary reads expensive and agent usage cumbersome.
Backfilling legacy prose may imply claim precision the original records never had.

initiatives.title: Change impact and invalidation engine
initiatives.outcome: A commit range produces an explainable set of directly and transitively affected claims, seams, findings, and obligations without invalidating unrelated knowledge.
initiatives.rationale: Precise impact is the economic hinge: too little recall makes the record unsafe, while excessive invalidation destroys the promised time savings.
deliverables: A predicted-diff artifact listing changed files, mapped objects, traversed relations, invalidated claims, and unaffected controls before comparison with expected results.
A deterministic impact cascade using file ledger, evidence links, explicit cross-references, seam endpoints, and git rename data.
A pluggable escalation point for lexical or model-assisted relation discovery only when explicit relations leave a measured gap.
An impact explanation API and durable invalidation events.
acceptance: The known-invalidation fixture reaches the expected claim and downstream obligation with no hidden manual expansion.
The benign-refactor fixture stays within the false-invalidation guardrail and explains every invalidated object.
Two-sided sensitivity checks show that adding and removing each relation class changes impact output in the predicted direction.
The explicit-relation implementation is measured before any model or embedding fallback is admitted.
initiatives.redGate: Remove a required cross-reference or seam edge from the fixture; the predicted impact must lose the corresponding downstream claim and the coverage gate must turn red.
risks: Static relations can miss runtime coupling and generated-code dependencies.
Model-assisted impact can create nondeterministic invalidation noise.

initiatives.title: Obligation-driven revalidation scheduler
initiatives.outcome: Invalidated knowledge becomes a bounded, prioritized queue whose completed work lands back into the conspectus and whose omissions remain visibly red.
initiatives.rationale: Detection without custody only creates a better stale list. Full automation requires a closed loop from change to assigned work to verified landing.
deliverables: A durable obligation table with trigger, destination, owner, blocking state, resolution evidence, and attempt history.
A scheduler that scopes work packets from invalidated claims and their evidence neighborhoods, with budgets and retry policy.
Dispatched/landed/scored reconciliation and dead-letter handling.
Dashboard views for blocked, retried, deferred, and orphaned obligations.
acceptance: Every invalidated authoritative claim creates at least one owned destination or a hard failure explaining why none can be formed.
A dropped, duplicated, timed-out, or unscored worker result prevents run completion and remains queryable.
Retries use unique attempt and replicate identifiers; a retry cannot overwrite earlier evidence.
The scheduler stays within configured source, budget, concurrency, and authority boundaries during an unattended fixture run.
initiatives.redGate: Silently drop one dispatched obligation and duplicate another; completion must remain red with separate missing and duplicate diagnoses.
risks: Queue throughput can become a proxy target that rewards shallow closures.
Aggressive retries can amplify provider cost or repeat correlated errors.

initiatives.title: Verified resolution and projection read-back
initiatives.outcome: Fixed, revalidated, and materialized become evidenced states rather than optimistic labels.
initiatives.rationale: The current asymmetry—proof required to rule out but not to mark fixed—undercuts the core claim that users should not have to redo verification.
deliverables: Distinct fixed-pending-verification and verified-fixed states with repository-SHA-bound confirming evidence.
Resolution invariants for findings, claims, contradictions, and obligations.
A clean materialization mode followed by state, coverage, and content read-back.
A repair path that records projection mismatch without modifying durable truth to match the projection.
acceptance: A fix-location-only update cannot reach verified-fixed.
Evidence from before the repair commit cannot verify the repaired state.
Deleting a rendered finding, cross-link, or stale marker is detected by the appropriate read-back axis.
Historical fixed and invalidated states remain auditable after later supersession.
initiatives.redGate: Mark a known finding fixed without post-fix evidence and remove one rendered object; both the state transition and publish step must halt.
risks: A universal proof rule may not fit every finding class.
Read-back can validate correspondence while still missing a semantically bad source claim.

initiatives.title: Unattended refresh run envelope
initiatives.outcome: A fully surveyed repository can be refreshed end to end from a commit range with deterministic controls, bounded provider use, explicit stop conditions, and a complete audit trail.
initiatives.rationale: Full automation is a systems property. It requires authority, idempotence, reconciliation, and recovery—not just a prompt that continues without asking.
deliverables: A refresh command/API with plan, execute, resume, cancel, and read-back states.
An execution manifest pinning repository SHA, source set, model/runtime configuration, budgets, determinism settings, and unique run/replicate IDs.
Idempotency and crash-recovery contracts for every mutating stage.
Authority-policy enforcement for configured providers, data boundaries, decision gates, code mutation, and external side effects.
acceptance: An interrupted run resumes without duplicated authoritative claims or lost obligations.
A determinism control actually changes the consulted runtime path and is visible in the run manifest.
Configured analysis providers run without interactive approval while out-of-envelope providers or side effects stop before dispatch.
The final status is computed from durable landed state and read-back, never from worker success messages.
initiatives.redGate: Crash after dispatch and before landing, then resume; if work duplicates, disappears, or completion relies on the pre-crash success signal, A5 fails.
risks: Provider APIs differ in determinism, retries, and data retention.
A permissive default envelope could turn analysis automation into unauthorized action.

stages.label: Next — earn super review and architecture
stages.horizon: Following 8–14 engineering weeks, gated on the living-record exit rather than elapsed time.
stages.objective: Turn the current conspectus into high-density review and design instruments without blurring evidence, intent, recommendation, or authority.
exitCriteria: A known historical defect, a cross-seam defect, and a benign refactor produce the expected differentiated review behavior.
Review briefs reduce median human verification time while meeting actionable-precision and missed-contract gates.
An incoherent design request is returned as underdetermined with the missing desire or evidence named.
A design session preserves explicit constraints and non-consensus options through decision-record read-back.
The integral HEAD lane catches a seeded composition failure that all subsystem-local checks miss.

initiatives.title: Impact-aware review brief
initiatives.outcome: A reviewer receives the smallest sufficient situation model for a change: diff, affected claims, constraints, history, seams, contradictions, obligations, and explicit unknowns.
initiatives.rationale: The product's value is not more context; it is the right evidence and prior work arranged around the current decision.
deliverables: A typed ReviewBrief contract with included and omitted sections, provenance, token budget, and repository validity.
A context compiler that uses explicit impact relations first and logs every inclusion and exclusion reason.
Views for historical confirmed/ruled-out findings, compensating controls, stale claims, cross-seam obligations, and unverified areas.
A task-scoped retrieval trace suitable for later method evaluation.
acceptance: The known-defect fixture includes the prior finding and current supporting evidence; the benign refactor does not inherit unrelated defect context.
Removing the task constraint, impacted seam, or stale-claim section changes the brief's control score in the predicted direction.
Every compressed statement expands to typed claims and evidence valid at the reviewed commit.
The brief declares uncovered files, omitted sections, and budget-driven truncation before recommendations.
initiatives.redGate: Supply a diff whose only known risk is in an affected seam; if the seam obligation is omitted or appears without provenance, publication halts.
risks: Task-focused compression may hide a weak but important cross-cutting signal.
Retrieval quality can be confused with underlying record quality.

initiatives.title: Independent review generation and refutation
initiatives.outcome: Candidate review findings are generated and attacked by role-separated passes with controlled context differences, then aggregated without contaminating independent judgments.
initiatives.rationale: A large context and a self-critique prompt do not create independent scrutiny. Consequential findings need a refutation path designed around correlated failure.
deliverables: Generator, refuter, and verifier role contracts with different evidence access and no pre-aggregation deliberation.
A context-set diversity policy that varies evidence slices and analytical frames, not just role labels.
Blind fixtures using surface-identical marker/control cases and treated-versus-clean diffs.
An aggregation record retaining disagreements, defeated hypotheses, and the evidence that moved status.
acceptance: A refuter can overturn a seeded false positive only by attaching new disproving evidence.
Independent passes land before aggregation and cannot read each other's conclusions during judgment.
Marker-only and treated-versus-clean controls remain blinded through scoring and do not produce directional contamination.
Same-context, varied-context, and heterogeneous-runtime conditions are reported separately with test-retest stability.
initiatives.redGate: Reveal expected findings or another pass's verdict to a blinded reviewer; the harness must mark the run contaminated and exclude it from efficacy claims.
risks: Nominal agent separation may preserve correlated context and model errors.
Extra passes can increase cost without improving decision quality.

initiatives.title: Composition and integral HEAD verification
initiatives.outcome: The review system proves that expected parts landed, fans in results, and evaluates the assembled repository state rather than inferring integration from local successes.
initiatives.rationale: Many consequential failures live at seams or appear only after individually correct patches compose.
deliverables: A fan-in manifest reconciling expected artifacts, commits, tests, and review results.
An integral HEAD lane with seam-specific concern selection and clean-checkout execution.
A seeded cross-seam defect corpus whose local checks pass while the integral lane fails.
Blocking status propagation from missing or failed composition obligations.
acceptance: The seeded cross-seam defect is missed by both subsystem-local lanes and caught by the integral lane.
A worker success message without its expected artifact or commit keeps the fan-in gate red.
Every deferred composition concern has a named destination and remains visible in the final review.
The integral result is tied to the exact assembled HEAD SHA and cannot be reused for another state.
initiatives.redGate: Remove one expected landed artifact and seed one seam-only defect; both must independently block the final green state.
risks: Integral checks can become an expensive duplicate of existing CI.
A narrow seeded corpus may overstate composition coverage.

initiatives.title: Review session and export surface
initiatives.outcome: A user can ask what changed, what matters, what survived challenge, and what remains unknown, then inspect every answer without learning the internal schema.
initiatives.rationale: A rigorous record that cannot furnish a fast decision surface fails the original make-it-make-sense-without-wasting-time promise.
deliverables: Review-session commands for situation, findings, challenges, regressions, latent defects, stale knowledge, and open obligations.
A compact default brief plus progressive evidence expansion.
A clean export with stable identifiers and bidirectional links to durable records.
A review completion record that distinguishes advice furnished from decisions accepted.
acceptance: A reviewer can reach cited evidence for every actionable claim in no more than one expansion step.
Regression, pre-existing latent defect, ruled-out historical finding, and unverified suspicion are rendered as distinct states.
Export read-back reconciles state, coverage, and content against the source run.
User testing measures verification minutes and missed constraints, not satisfaction alone.
initiatives.redGate: Swap the labels for regression and latent defect or remove an unknown from the export; semantic read-back must detect the mismatch.
risks: A dense default view can become another dashboard users ignore.
Progressive disclosure may hide uncertainty behind an extra click.

initiatives.title: CodebaseBrief architecture contract
initiatives.outcome: Review, design, and generative sessions consume a stable, task-bounded codebase situation model rather than reaching directly into storage tables.
initiatives.rationale: A shared contract concentrates epistemic discipline and creates the future seam with Chorusmith without giving Chorusmith custody of Amanuensis truth.
deliverables: A versioned CodebaseBrief schema covering facts, direct intent, inferred intent, constraints, contradictions, changes, options, gaps, provenance, and validity.
Mode-specific projections for review, design, and generative work.
Budget and omission semantics with deterministic registry/lexical selection before model-assisted compilation.
Contract fixtures independent of the SQLite implementation.
acceptance: The same source record produces mode-specific briefs without changing source truth.
Direct intent, inferred intent, observed behavior, and recommendation remain distinguishable after serialization and read-back.
Every omission is represented by policy, irrelevance, or budget reason; silent truncation fails.
A registry lookup handles explicit object identity without a model call.
initiatives.redGate: Round-trip a brief after deleting epistemic-kind or omission metadata; schema or semantic validation must reject it.
risks: A prematurely broad contract can freeze accidental storage concepts.
Mode projections can drift into separate products.

initiatives.title: Dialectical design-session engine
initiatives.outcome: Amanuensis furnishes immanent, adversarial, and speculative design lenses, preserves their disagreements, and returns a lean with falsifiers rather than an artificial consensus.
initiatives.rationale: Architecture support should expose potential and tension while remaining anchored to actual code and user desire.
deliverables: Three independent lens prompts/contracts with controlled context sets and content-blinded evaluation fixtures.
An option matrix covering preserves, rejects, enables, forecloses, migration cost, reversibility, and evidence gaps.
A lean that cites decisive evidence, surviving disagreement, falsifiers, and research needs.
An underdetermination response that asks for a missing desire or labels evidence gaps instead of inventing a goal.
acceptance: An incoherent request produces a named contradiction or missing desire rather than a confident architecture.
The three lenses are generated independently before aggregation and retain at least one meaningful disagreement in the seeded dialectical fixture.
Removing a stated constraint worsens constraint-preservation scoring; restoring it improves the score.
A recommendation cannot be accepted as a decision without an authorized acceptance event.
initiatives.redGate: Give the engine mutually exclusive goals with no priority rule; any unqualified single recommendation fails the underdetermination gate.
risks: Named lenses can become theatrical personas rather than genuinely different analyses.
A persuasive lean may still dominate human choice despite formal authority boundaries.

initiatives.title: Decision custody and consequence tracking
initiatives.outcome: Accepted architecture decisions, rejected options, consequences, and falsifiers become durable context without converting model proposals into policy.
initiatives.rationale: A system that remembers code but forgets why it changed will repeatedly reopen settled choices or mistake an implementation accident for intent.
deliverables: Draft, accepted, rejected, superseded, and invalidated decision states with explicit acceptance authority.
Links from decisions to desires, claims, constraints, alternatives, code changes, consequences, and falsifiers.
Decision-impact detection that creates review obligations when code or evidence undermines an accepted premise.
A portable decision projection for Chorusmith session custody without transferring source authority.
acceptance: A generated recommendation remains draft until an authorized acceptance event names the accepter and scope.
A changed premise creates a visible decision-review obligation and does not silently rewrite the original decision.
Rejected options remain queryable with their evidence and can be reconsidered only as a new revision.
Read-back preserves desire source, acceptance authority, alternatives, and falsifiers.
initiatives.redGate: Attempt to promote a model-authored draft without authorized acceptance or silently edit an accepted decision's premise; both writes must fail.
risks: Decision records can become bureaucratic and lag real practice.
A stale accepted decision can exert undue authority unless premise invalidation is reliable.

stages.label: Later — close the research-learning loop and compose with Chorusmith
stages.horizon: After review and design modes meet their gates on more than one repository; sequence by evidence, not date.
stages.objective: Let Amanuensis ask for, ingest, and learn from external research and completed sessions while retaining strict custody and attribution boundaries.
exitCriteria: Research questions are admitted only when they name a decision, uncertainty, evidence need, and destination.
Imported research retains Scholiast provenance and cannot become a code fact without repository evidence.
Candidate method lessons are promoted only after qualification, validation, and read-back.
Research decision yield is positive without an unbounded backlog or degraded human verification time.
A Chorusmith adapter demonstrates behavior and evidence parity before any workflow extraction.

initiatives.title: Research-question broker
initiatives.outcome: Amanuensis emits bounded research requests only when external knowledge could resolve a named architecture or review uncertainty.
initiatives.rationale: Continuous topic generation without admission criteria produces intellectual exhaust, not learning.
deliverables: A ResearchRequest contract naming decision, current evidence, uncertainty, needed source class, disconfirmers, budget, and destination.
Admission rules for decision relevance, local-evidence exhaustion, expected information value, and duplication.
A durable queue with rejected, deferred, dispatched, landed, consumed, and expired states.
A result adapter that preserves source provenance and separates external claims from code observations.
acceptance: A curiosity-only topic with no decision destination is rejected or explicitly parked outside the blocking queue.
A duplicate question links to prior research instead of dispatching again unless changed premises are named.
A research result cannot become a code fact without repository evidence; it may alter a hypothesis, option, or decision premise.
Every consumed result records which decision field changed or why it changed nothing.
initiatives.redGate: Import a well-cited external claim that contradicts current code behavior; the system must preserve the contradiction and refuse to rewrite the code observation.
risks: Expected information value is hard to calibrate and easy to game.
Research latency can block decisions that should proceed under explicit uncertainty.

initiatives.title: Typed crosswalk and Collatio qualification
initiatives.outcome: External research, code claims, concerns, decisions, and methods connect through explicit supported relations, and new methods must pass qualification before entering unattended workflows.
initiatives.rationale: Cross-domain learning fails when resemblance is treated as identity or when an attractive technique bypasses control testing.
deliverables: A typed crosswalk relation set with provenance, validity, counterevidence, and negative criteria.
Identity-before-enrichment resolution for imported resources and methods.
A Collatio qualification adapter covering prediction, controls, red-gate demonstration, and result custody.
Crosswalk-specific contradiction and supersession handling.
acceptance: Two similarly named concepts do not merge without an identity relation and supporting evidence.
A method cannot enter the unattended policy registry until its predicted effect, controls, and red gate are recorded and passed.
A contradictory external source remains attached as counterevidence rather than being averaged into consensus.
Generated projections reproduce crosswalk counts, endpoints, relation types, and unresolved contradictions.
initiatives.redGate: Present a surface-similar but semantically distinct pair; automatic identity merge or inherited properties fail the gate.
risks: A bespoke relation vocabulary can grow into an ontology project.
Strict qualification can reject useful low-risk heuristics whose value is hard to measure.

initiatives.title: Distillation and revisable learning ledger
initiatives.outcome: Completed review and design sessions yield candidate lessons about corpus, retrieval, method, research, and user preference, each promoted only with evidence and a rollback path.
initiatives.rationale: The system should improve from use, but an untyped memory update would blend truth, workflow convenience, and transient preference into irreversible policy.
deliverables: Five separate learning channels: corpus, retrieval, method, research, and user preference.
A candidate-to-qualified-to-active-to-superseded lifecycle with provenance and evaluation evidence.
Session-outcome extraction that compares planned, produced, accepted, and later-invalidated artifacts.
A read-back audit that proves policy/configuration changes landed where the next run actually reads them.
acceptance: An unscored session can produce candidate lessons but cannot activate a method or preference.
A learned preference records its human source and scope and cannot masquerade as a code or research fact.
A promoted method shows an outcome change under treatment-versus-clean or ablation controls before activation.
Superseding a lesson preserves prior versions and identifies affected future runs.
initiatives.redGate: Write an attractive session summary directly into active policy; the write path must reject the missing qualification and read-back evidence.
risks: Sparse feedback can make method-learning claims underpowered.
User preferences may be contextual and become harmful when generalized.

initiatives.title: Multi-repository evaluation and operating envelope
initiatives.outcome: The product has an explicit evidence-backed operating envelope across repository types, change classes, review modes, and model/runtime configurations.
initiatives.rationale: One successful self-survey or showcase repository is an existence proof, not a basis for general automation claims.
deliverables: A stratified corpus of repositories and seeded/known outcomes with explicit inclusion and exclusion criteria.
Preregistered per-condition metrics, minimum detectable effects, replicate counts, and stopping rules.
Independent context/model conditions, nulls, graded controls, two-sided sensitivity checks, and component ablations.
An operating-envelope report that names unsupported languages, scales, repository shapes, and decision classes.
Raw agreement, chance agreement, and chance-corrected agreement reported together whenever a kappa statistic is used.
acceptance: Results are reported per repository, mode, model/runtime configuration, and replicate; no pooled headline hides subgroup failures.
Every efficacy claim includes a verified baseline, null, stronger control, ablation, and test-retest result.
Negative results clear instrument delivery and determinism before lowering the product claim.
Positive results survive an adversarial alternative-explanation pass and preserve excluded observations in every metric.

Ceiling, floor, or no-headroom conditions produce an undetermined-instrument verdict rather than a null, and an unused rubric category receives an operational-framing check before it is attributed to the model.
initiatives.redGate: Pool a weak subgroup into a positive aggregate or reuse a replicate ID; the report generator must reject publication.
risks: A representative corpus is expensive and can still miss deployment-specific conditions.
Benchmarks may become targets and displace actual verification-time reduction.

initiatives.title: Chorusmith adapter and parity-gated extraction
initiatives.outcome: Chorusmith can orchestrate Amanuensis as a codebase project type through stable contracts, while Amanuensis remains independently usable and its invariants stay authoritative.
initiatives.rationale: General orchestration belongs in Chorusmith, but early extraction would trade a working domain workflow for an unproven platform abstraction.
deliverables: Versioned adapters for CodebaseBrief, ReviewBrief, ResearchRequest, Decision, Obligation, and Run manifests.
Contract and replay tests that run the same scenarios directly and through Chorusmith.
A custody matrix for durable truth, session artifacts, provider configuration, and user preferences.
An extraction ADR with rollback and a feature-by-feature parity ledger.
acceptance: Direct and orchestrated runs reconcile the same authoritative claims, obligations, decisions, and evidence identifiers.
Chorusmith cannot bypass Amanuensis evidence, depth, authority, or completion gates.
Amanuensis remains runnable without Chorusmith and produces an equivalent clean export for the parity corpus.
No workflow moves until behavior, evidence, recovery, and verification-time parity pass.
initiatives.redGate: Bypass an Amanuensis invariant through the adapter or remove Chorusmith mid-run; the former must be rejected and the latter must resume without source-state corruption.
risks: Contract duplication can ossify both projects.
Parity may conceal usability regressions or operational complexity.

firstSlices.title: Freeze definitions and build the red-gate harness
firstSlices.intent: Create the fixture and checkers before changing persistence. This slice predicts every expected failure and proves the harness can observe it.
proves: The operational definition of fully surveyed is computable.
Each completion and correspondence gate can visibly fail.
The measurement harness can distinguish null, benign, invalidating, seam, and incoherent-request cases.
requiredChecks: Run the new control test with every sabotage case enabled individually.
Run existing invariants, adversarial-correctness, and materializer tests.
Rebuild the fixture in a clean temporary directory and read it back.
firstSlices.rollback: Remove the fixture, ADR, checker, and test wiring; retain or separately revert the WAL checkpoint repair according to its regression test.

firstSlices.title: Add temporal claims without replacing legacy records
firstSlices.intent: Introduce the minimum temporal substrate additively, expose it behind explicit tools, and keep legacy projections working until parity is measured.
proves: Current authority can be queried at a commit without deleting history.
Epistemic kinds and evidence gates are server-enforced.
Existing databases and tools remain usable during migration.
requiredChecks: Run bounded exhaustive interval, cycle, and reachability tests.
Run schema identifier, tool-schema, smoke, storage, and invariant suites.
Compare legacy and compatibility projections on the pinned self-conspectus.
firstSlices.rollback: Leave additive tables unused and revert tool registration; do not destructively down-migrate existing databases.

firstSlices.title: Predict and explain change impact
firstSlices.intent: Replace subsystem-wide stale marking as the only mechanism with an explainable explicit-relation cascade, while retaining the coarse path as a safe fallback.
proves: Known invalidations propagate through explicit dependencies.
Benign changes do not erase unrelated current knowledge.
Every impact result is accompanied by a traversable reason path.
requiredChecks: Record the predicted diff before comparing fixture outcomes.
Run two-sided edge addition/removal sensitivity checks and an explicit-relation ablation.
Run existing git, storage, comparison, performance, and adversarial suites.
firstSlices.rollback: Switch the impact policy back to conservative subsystem invalidation; retain emitted validity events for audit.

firstSlices.title: Close the obligation loop
firstSlices.intent: Turn invalidations into durable work with explicit ownership, fan-in reconciliation, retry identity, and stop conditions.
proves: Dispatched, landed, and scored work reconcile before completion.
Retries and partial failures remain auditable.
requiredChecks: Inject loss, duplication, timeout, and unscored-result faults independently.
Verify unique run, work-item, attempt, and replicate identifiers.
Run cloud E2E, autoprogress, locks, invariants, and performance ceilings.
firstSlices.rollback: Disable automatic dispatch and leave obligations visible for manual processing; never mark them resolved during rollback.

firstSlices.title: Require proof of repair and verify the clean export
firstSlices.intent: Make resolution symmetric with refutation and validate derived artifacts along state, coverage, and content axes.
proves: Fixed is not confused with verified-fixed.
Pre-fix evidence cannot certify post-fix behavior.
A published projection corresponds to durable source state.
requiredChecks: Demonstrate both state-transition and projection-corruption gates red.
Render into a clean temporary directory before read-back.
Run all finding, evidence, materializer, storage-history, and adversarial tests.
firstSlices.rollback: Retain the stricter states in storage but disable publication of verified-fixed; fall back to fixed-pending-verification rather than weakening the evidence rule.

firstSlices.title: Ship the bounded unattended refresh
firstSlices.intent: Compose plan, impact, obligations, workers, landing, scoring, and read-back into one resumable run with explicit authority and provider boundaries.
proves: A living conspectus can maintain itself across a real commit range.
Configured APIs run unattended while expanded authority stops before dispatch.
Crash recovery and final read-back preserve source-state integrity.
requiredChecks: Run crash injection at every mutating boundary and resume each case.
Verify the determinism knob changes an observed runtime input.
Run the complete repository suite and compare refresh versus full-resurvey verification minutes.
firstSlices.rollback: Disable unattended execution while retaining plan and impact generation; all unfinished obligations remain blocking and visible.

metrics.name: Survey completion integrity
metrics.definition: Required obligations present and valid divided by all obligations required by the pinned inventory, concern, seam, run, and export manifests.
metrics.target: 100%; any missing blocking obligation keeps completion red.
metrics.exclusions: Files and concerns explicitly excluded before execution with owner and reason remain in the denominator as satisfied exclusions; post-hoc exclusions are forbidden.

metrics.name: Stale-claim recall
metrics.definition: Expected invalidated authoritative claims reached by the impact engine divided by all invalidated claims in the labeled fixture.
metrics.target: ≥95% before targeted invalidation replaces the conservative fallback; 100% for critical seeded claims.
metrics.exclusions: Unlabeled claims and changes outside the pinned commit range are reported separately, not silently removed.

metrics.name: False invalidation rate
metrics.definition: Still-valid authoritative claims withdrawn by the impact engine divided by all still-valid claims in the benign and mixed fixtures.
metrics.target: ≤10% initially and lower than conservative subsystem invalidation by a preregistered margin.
metrics.exclusions: Claims whose validity cannot be adjudicated stay unknown and are not counted as true negatives.

metrics.name: Human revalidation reduction
metrics.definition: One minus targeted-refresh active human verification minutes divided by full-resurvey active human verification minutes for the same repository state and quality gates; machine wall time, provider cost, and token use are reported alongside as separate units.
metrics.target: >30% human-time reduction with no decrease in M2 or known-defect recall before living refresh is the default; machine cost must remain within the A0-preregistered guardrail.
metrics.exclusions: Setup and cache warm-up are included for both paths; failed or abandoned runs remain in reported time and cost.

metrics.name: Actionable precision
metrics.definition: Review findings accepted as correctly evidenced and action-relevant divided by all review findings presented as actionable.
metrics.target: ≥80% on the evaluation corpus, reported by severity and finding class.
metrics.exclusions: Unverified suspicions are a separate product output and cannot be removed from the review-volume report.

metrics.name: Missed-contract rate
metrics.definition: Known applicable contracts absent from the review brief or integral assessment divided by all applicable labeled contracts.
metrics.target: 0 for critical contracts and <5% overall before super review is recommended for consequential changes.
metrics.exclusions: Unsupported languages or repository regions remain explicit unsupported strata, not exclusions from the headline.

metrics.name: Human verification minutes
metrics.definition: Elapsed active human time from furnished brief to accept, reject, or correctly defer the review or design output.
metrics.target: Lower median than repository-native review with non-inferior correctness; report distribution and repository strata.
metrics.exclusions: Training, interruption, and tool-failure time are tagged and reported both included and separated.

metrics.name: Constraint preservation
metrics.definition: Explicit user, code, operational, and compatibility constraints retained correctly through brief, option matrix, lean, and decision projection divided by all stated constraints.
metrics.target: 100% for hard constraints; soft constraints may be traded only with an explicit consequence.
metrics.exclusions: Contradictory constraints stay in the denominator and require an underdetermination result.

metrics.name: Unknown retention
metrics.definition: Known gaps and unresolved contradictions visible with a destination in the final artifact divided by those present in the source situation model.
metrics.exclusions: Resolved items require resolution evidence; compression alone is not resolution.

metrics.name: Research decision yield
metrics.definition: Consumed research requests that change a named option, premise, confidence reason, or decision divided by all completed research requests.
metrics.target: Establish baseline first; rescope admission if yield stays below 20% for two evaluation cycles while backlog grows.
metrics.exclusions: Explicit exploratory research is reported separately and cannot improve the decision-yield numerator.

metrics.name: Test-retest stability
metrics.definition: Across at least two runs with identical pinned inputs: exact agreement on critical status and blocking-obligation IDs, plus Jaccard agreement on noncritical authoritative object IDs; report both components and metric step size.
metrics.target: No critical-status disagreement; quantitative target set after A0 baseline rather than invented in advance.
metrics.exclusions: Runs with different model/runtime configuration, context set, or determinism input are separate conditions.

metrics.name: Run and projection reconciliation
metrics.definition: Expected work and durable objects that are dispatched, landed, scored, materialized, and read back consistently divided by all expected work and objects.
metrics.exclusions: Canceled work remains present with an authorized cancellation state and is never erased from the denominator.

controlLadder.expected: No authoritative claim is invalidated; repeated runs remain separately identifiable and materially stable.
Marker presence alone does not create directional review or design effects.
Evidence locations repair or invalidate narrowly; unrelated claims remain current.

controlLadder.fixture: Known historical defect at its original and repaired commits
controlLadder.expected: The original review surfaces the prior confirmed finding; the repaired revision distinguishes fixed-pending-verification from verified-fixed and never relabels the history as a new regression.
The exact claim loses authority, receives an obligation, and cannot recover without new evidence.
Local checks stay green, impact crosses the seam, and the integral HEAD lane blocks completion.

controlLadder.fixture: Mutually incompatible design goals without priority
controlLadder.expected: The session returns underdetermined, preserves both goals, and requests human desire rather than choosing silently.

controlLadder.fixture: Corrupted clean export and missing landed result
controlLadder.expected: State, coverage, content, and fan-in checks independently turn red and name the mismatch.

risks.risk: The product becomes a general knowledge platform and loses its code-evidence advantage.
risks.signal: Roadmap work adds generic orchestration, ontology, or collaboration infrastructure before M2–M7 improve.
risks.mitigation: Require every Amanuensis feature to improve a named codebase decision metric; move general session machinery behind a Chorusmith contract.

risks.risk: The living record is either unsafe or as expensive as a resurvey.
risks.signal: M2 misses critical invalidations, M3 invalidates most claims, or M4 stays below its gate.
risks.mitigation: Keep the conservative fallback, narrow the supported operating envelope, and stop downstream feature expansion.

risks.risk: Automation hides uncertainty behind a green status.
risks.signal: Blocking unknowns, dropped work, projection mismatches, or provider failures disappear from final artifacts.
risks.mitigation: Make obligations, reconciliation, and read-back server-side halting gates with sabotage tests.

risks.risk: Architecture assistance invents intent or entrenches accidental structure.
risks.signal: Inferred intent is rendered as direct intent or recommendations survive contradictory goals without qualification.
risks.mitigation: Typed epistemic kinds, underdetermination tests, three non-consensus lenses, and human acceptance authority.

risks.risk: Research and learning loops optimize volume rather than decisions.
risks.signal: Backlog grows while M10 falls, or unscored sessions change active policy.
risks.mitigation: Admission criteria, decision destinations, qualification, ablation, and reversible learning states.

risks.risk: Evaluation results are attractive but not transportable.
risks.signal: Claims rely on one repository, pooled metrics, shared context, or a single run.
risks.mitigation: Stratified corpora, independent conditions, unique replicates, MDEs, nulls, graded controls, and explicit operating envelopes.

killCriteria.trigger: Targeted refresh fails critical stale-claim recall or does not reduce verification work after two bounded design iterations
killCriteria.action: Stop review/design expansion; retain Amanuensis as a high-integrity survey and conservative resurvey tool while reconsidering the impact model.

killCriteria.trigger: The durable record does not lower human verification minutes at non-inferior correctness
killCriteria.action: Remove or radically simplify the system-of-record claim; optimize the brief and evidence path before adding capabilities.

killCriteria.trigger: Review, design, and generative modes cannot preserve epistemic-kind separation in blinded scoring
killCriteria.action: Do not ship the affected mode; keep it as an explicitly experimental lens outside authoritative output.

killCriteria.trigger: Research backlog grows for two evaluation cycles while decision yield remains below 20%
killCriteria.action: Disable automatic dispatch, retain manual research requests, and tighten admission or remove the loop.

killCriteria.trigger: Chorusmith orchestration fails behavior, evidence, recovery, or verification-time parity
killCriteria.action: Do not extract the workflow; keep the adapter experimental and Amanuensis independently complete.

killCriteria.trigger: A provider, model, or graph layer adds cost without surviving its ablation
killCriteria.action: Remove it and return to the simpler explicit-relation or deterministic implementation.

applied.use: Evidence-first definitions, explicit observation/inference/open-question separation, provenance, operational definitions, and baseline verification.
applied.verification: A0 and A1 make these durable and reject unsupported authority; this roadmap labels its own baseline by epistemic kind.

applied.use: Mechanical halting gates, red-gate demonstrations, fan-in reconciliation, determinism delivery, clean export, and three-axis read-back.
applied.verification: Every initiative has a red gate; A0, A3–A5, A8–A10, and A17 name the machine checks that block completion.

applied.use: Contradictions, deferrals, and invalidations remain durable first-class obligations with explicit destinations.
applied.verification: The minimum durable objects include validity and obligation lifecycles; M1, M9, and M12 keep gaps in the denominator.

applied.use: Authority is designed into unattended automation; desire and decision acceptance remain human-owned.
applied.verification: The authority section and A5/A11/A12 red gates reject unauthorized provider expansion and automatic decision acceptance.

applied.use: Single-responsibility generation/refutation/verification, context-set diversity, heterogeneous resolving-profile conditions without an assumed quality premium, surface-identical nulls, treated-versus-clean marker checks, and adversarial follow-up.
applied.verification: A7, A11, and A16 specify independence before aggregation, role boundaries, contamination failure, blinded scoring, and separate model/context condition reports.

applied.use: Task-shaped briefs, domain-calibrated concerns, deterministic registry/lexical paths first, bounded exhaustive checks for relational cores, and predicted diffs before comparison.
applied.verification: A1/A2 test relation cores exhaustively and require predicted impact diffs; A6/A10 log context inclusions and forbid model calls for explicit lookup; A16 stratifies domains.

applied.use: Composition is independently verified with fan-in, an integral HEAD lane, graded controls, two-sided sensitivity, and ablation before attribution.
applied.verification: A2 and A8 require predicted relation effects, seam-only defects, missing-artifact sabotage, and explicit-relation/provider ablations.

applied.use: Metrics are actor-sensitive, specifically attributed, exclusion-stable, uniquely replicated, separately reported, and powered before efficacy runs; agreement reports raw and chance components, unused labels are operationalized, and no-headroom results remain undetermined-instrument rather than null.
applied.verification: A0 and A16 require replicate identities, MDEs, framing checks, headroom verdicts, and complete agreement reporting; the measurement contract defines denominators, exclusions, strata, and non-pooling.

limitations: This roadmap was authored and adversarially re-read in one agent context; it is not an independent or blinded validation of the product thesis. A7 and A16 require real independence before efficacy claims.
Numeric gates for recall, invalidation, and precision are initial operating hypotheses, not established effect estimates; A0 and A16 may revise them with recorded rationale.

The roadmap validator proves structure, dependency integrity, required fields, practice-accounting coverage, evidence-path existence, and projection correspondence. It does not prove that roadmap claims are true or that the plan will work.
External Chorusmith, Scholiast, Collatio, and distillation contracts were used as planning context but are not vendored or enforced by this repository yet.
